new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made it possible to appoint the same person as Governor of two or more States?
new.x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 added a proviso to Article 153 so that one person can be Governor of two or more States.
new.angle: U0313 #4/#11 Same Governor for two States -> amendment

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution makes the Governor an integral part of the State Legislature?
new.x: Article 168 says the State Legislature consists of the Governor and the House or Houses; he is part of it without being a member.
new.angle: U0313 notes gap Art 168 Governor part of legislature

new.s: On whose opinion does the Governor decide whether a member of the State Legislature has become disqualified under Article 192?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: Under Article 192 the Governor decides non-defection disqualification, but he must act on the opinion of the Election Commission.
new.angle: U0313 APPSC PYQ yd8d306a73c6 Art 192 disqualification -> decided by

new.s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Governor summon, prorogue and dissolve the State Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Article 174 lets the Governor summon and prorogue the Houses and dissolve the Assembly; 175-176 deal with addresses, 213 with ordinances.
new.angle: U0313 APPSC PYQ yd2a077fe139 dissolution of Assembly -> Governor (#5)

new.s: When does an ordinance promulgated by the Governor cease to operate if it is not approved?
o: Three months after the State Legislature reassembles
At the end of the financial year
Six weeks after the State Legislature reassembles
Six months after it is promulgated
new.x: A Governor's ordinance under Article 213 lapses six weeks after the State Legislature reassembles, unless disapproved earlier.
new.angle: U0313 #5 Ordinance power (Art 213) -> lapse

new.s: Who among the following reports to the President on the administration of the Scheduled Areas in a State under the Fifth Schedule?
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
new.x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Governor reports to the President on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the State.
new.angle: U0313 APPSC PYQ y84ae64cd90c Scheduled Area -> Governor's role

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 163:
1. No court can inquire into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor.
2. The Governor's decision on whether a matter is within his discretion is final.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Article 163(3) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice, and Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on his discretion final.
new.angle: U0313 APPSC PYQ y5f61877b413 Art 163 orders open/closed to review (#2/#12)

new.s: In which year did the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations submit its report?
new.x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up in June 1983 and submitted its report in 1988.
new.angle: U0313 #3/#24 Commission on Governor -> year

new.s: Who was the first Governor of West Bengal?
new.x: C. Rajagopalachari was the first Governor of West Bengal; Padmaja Naidu was its first woman Governor.
new.angle: U0313 #17 FIRST Governors -> state

new.s: For how long can a person who is not a member of the State Legislature hold office as a Minister?
new.x: Under Article 164(4) a non-member Minister ceases to hold office after six consecutive months unless he becomes a member.
new.angle: U0314 #1 Non-member CM or minister -> time limit

new.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
new.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
new.angle: U0314 #5 AP FIRSTs -> Andhra State CM

new.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
new.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was the first Chief Minister of Hyderabad State.
new.angle: U0314 #5 FIRSTs -> Hyderabad State CM

new.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation in 2014?
new.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu became the first Chief Minister of residuary Andhra Pradesh in 2014.
new.angle: U0314 #5 AP FIRSTs -> residuary AP CM

new.s: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister in India?
new.x: E.M.S. Namboodiripad of Kerala was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.
new.angle: U0314 notes gap FIRST non-Congress CM

new.s: In which year did Mayawati first become the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh?
new.x: Mayawati first became UP Chief Minister in 1995; by May 2002 she had become CM three times.
new.angle: U0314 APPSC PYQ ye9626b99221/y60d63f36b98 Mayawati CM terms angle

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assemblies?
new.x: Article 332 reserves seats for SCs and STs in State Assemblies; Article 330 does so for the Lok Sabha.
new.angle: U0315 notes gap Art 332 reservation in Assemblies

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment provides for reserving about one-third of the seats in State Legislative Assemblies for women?
new.x: The 106th Amendment, 2023 reserves about one-third of Assembly seats for women, to take effect after post-census delimitation.
new.angle: U0315 notes gap 106th Amendment women's reservation

new.s: What happens to a Bill that originates in the State Legislative Council and is rejected by the Legislative Assembly?
o: The Bill comes to an end
A joint sitting of both Houses is held
The Governor decides the fate of the Bill
The Council can pass it again after three months
new.x: A Bill from the Council that the Assembly rejects simply ends; States have no joint sitting.
new.angle: U0315 APPSC PYQ ybf47131fcc6/yc01129e8ec3/y70d3f9f581c Council Bill rejected by Assembly

new.s:
Consider the following statements about disagreement between the two Houses of a State Legislature:
1. There is no provision for a joint sitting of the two Houses.
2. On an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly, the Council can only delay it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: States have no joint sitting, and the Council's power over an ordinary Bill is only to delay it (3 + 1 months).
new.angle: U0315 #2/#11 Deadlock resolution, Council's delaying power

new.s: A law of Parliament under Article 169 creating or abolishing a Legislative Council is NOT deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of which Article?
new.x: Article 169 says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368, so Parliament passes it by simple majority.
new.angle: U0315 #6/#10 Art 169 -> Parliament's law, not Art 368

new.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, what was the strength fixed for the Telangana Legislative Council?
new.x: The Act gave Telangana a Council of 40 members; Andhra Pradesh got not more than 50, later raised to 58.
new.angle: U0315 APPSC PYQ y7065a87ea55 AP Reorganisation Act -> Council strength

new.s: To whom does the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly address his resignation?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: Under Article 179 the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker, and the Deputy Speaker to the Speaker.
new.angle: U0315 #4/#12 Speaker -> resignation addressed to whom

new.s: Who among the following can vote in the election of the President of India?
o: Nominated members of a State Legislative Assembly
Elected members of a State Legislative Assembly
Members of a State Legislative Council
new.x: Only elected MLAs (with elected MPs) form the electoral college for the President; MLCs and nominated members do not vote.
new.angle: U0315 APPSC PYQ y66f083e7585 MLAs/MLCs in Presidential election (#18)

new.s: How many seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes respectively in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Of the 175 seats in the AP Assembly, 29 are reserved for SCs and 7 for STs.
new.angle: U0316 #2 AP Assembly SC and ST reserved seats

new.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have after bifurcation?
